title: QCon London 2026: Rewriting All of Spotify's Code Base, All the Time
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/spotify-honk-rewrite/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773836087810.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Spotify's Jo Kelly-Fenton and Aleksandar Mitic discussed Honk, an AI-powered coding agent that enables code migrations across Spotify's codebase. The system improves migration, reducing timelines drastically and addressing complexities that traditional scripts could not. Key challenges included handling edge cases and standardizing the codebase to facilitate review processes.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: HubSpot’s Sidekick: Multi-Model AI Code Review with 90% Faster Feedback and 80% Engineer Approval
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>HubSpot engineers introduced Sidekick, an internal AI powered code review system that analyzes pull requests using large language models and filters feedback through a secondary “judge agent.” The system reduced time to first feedback on pull requests by about 90 percent and is now used across tens of thousands of internal pull requests.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: QCon London 2026: SBOMs Move From Best Practice to Legal Obligation as CRA Enforcement Looms
Presentation: Mobile Server-Driven UI at Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/mobile-server-driven-ui-scale/en/mediumimage/rafael-ring-medium-1772013795892.jpg"/><p>Rafael Ring discusses the architectural evolution of server-driven UI at Nubank, moving from static mobile binaries to a sophisticated scripted framework called Catalyst. He explains how they implemented a tree-walk interpreter in Flutter to render dynamic layouts and logic from JSON payloads.</p> <i>By Rafael Ring</i>

title: Java 26 Delivers Language Innovation, Library Improvements, Performance and Security
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/java26-released/en/headerimage/java-istock-image-01-1773831519530.jpg"/><p>Oracle has released version 26 of the Java programming language and virtual machine. As the first non-LTS release since JDK 25, the final feature set includes 10 JEPs, five of which are still progressing through the preview and incubator stages. This release focuses on Java library improvements, language innovation, performance and security.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Use<’lifetimes> For<’what>
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/rust-lifetimes-loans-polonius/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773681721405.jpg"/><p>At QCon London, TrueLayer engineer Ethan Brierley reframed Rust lifetimes using the Polonius borrow checker's mental model: lifetimes as sets of loans rather than regions of code. He built from borrow checker basics through variance and subtyping to higher-ranked lifetimes with serde, showing how the loans perspective makes previously confusing lifetime errors intuitive.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Blurring the Lines: Engineering & Data Teams in the Age of AI
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/engineering-data-teams/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773759596044.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Lada Indra, Head of Data Platform at Pleo, shared insights from his experience across high-scale data systems. He illustrated both the risks of poorly aligned teams and the practical strategies that organizations can adopt to bridge the gap.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: Article: Beyond Memory Safety: What Makes Rust Different – Lessons from Autonomous Robotics
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/practical-robustness-going-beyond-memory-safety-rust/en/headerimage/beyond-memory-safety-what-makes-rust-different-lessons-from-autonomous-robotics-header-1773646654979.jpg"/><p>This article explores that question through the lens of a real-world Rust project: a system responsible for controlling fleets of autonomous mobile robots. While Rust's memory safety is a strong foundation, its true power lies in the type system and ownership rules. The session will go beyond memory safety and explore ways to encode behavior and protocols directly into types.</p> <i>By Andy Brinkmeyer</i>

title: War in Iran Damages Multiple AWS Data Centers, Challenging Multi-AZ Assumptions
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/aws-multiaz-conflict-outage/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773671194784.jpg"/><p>Earlier this month, Iranian drone strikes damaged three AWS data centers in the UAE and Bahrain, causing outages and disruptions to multiple services. The events, which affected multiple facilities within the same AWS region, sparked discussion in the community about how geopolitical conflict can directly impact global cloud infrastructure and multi-AZ deployments.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Uncorking Queueing Bottlenecks with OpenTelemetry
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/queue-otel-observability/en/headerimage/header-1773741090866.jpeg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Julian Wreford and Oli Lane from Gearset showcased how distributed tracing and SLOs solve asynchronous observability gaps. By shifting from queue-size metrics to latency-based alerts, the team improved incident response. Key technical takeaways included using OpenTelemetry trace state for async duration tracking and wide events to uncover hidden architectural waste.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Ontology‐Driven Observability: Building the E2E Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/ontology-at-netflix/en/headerimage/java-istock-image-01-1773771443400.jpg"/><p>Prasanna Vijayanathan and Renzo Sanchez-Silva, both Engineers at Netflix, presented “Ontology‐Driven Observability: Building the E2E Knowledge Graph at Netflix Scale” at QCon London 2026, where they discussed the design and implementation of an end-to-end knowledge graph that models the Netflix user experience.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: QCon London 2026: From DVDs to Global Streaming How Netflix’s Commerce Architecture Actually Evolved
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/netflix-dvds-to-global-streaming/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773745066624.jpg"/><p>Dynamic principal engineer at Netflix, Kasia Trapszo, expertly navigates the evolution of the company’s commerce architecture from a DVD rental service to a global streaming giant. Her insights on pragmatic adaptations to billing systems reveal invaluable lessons on agility, localization, and the complexity of modern payment landscapes.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Reliable Retrieval for Production AI Systems
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/retrieval-production-ai/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773755451286.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Lan Chu, AI Tech Lead at Rabobank, shared lessons from deploying a production AI search system used internally by more than 300 users across 10,000 documents. Her experience shows that most failures in RAG systems stem from indexing and retrieval, rather than the language model itself.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Shipping Constantly with Humans and Beyond at Monzo
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/shipping-monzo/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773761561765.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Suhail Patel, a principal engineer at Monzo who leads the bank’s platform group, described how the bank has built a developer platform capable of shipping hundreds of changes to production every day.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: QCon London 2026: Managing Asynchronous APIs at Scale
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/03/managing-async-apis/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1773756314998.jpg"/><p>At QCon London 2026, Ian Cooper, senior principal engineer at Just Eat Takeaway, discussed managing asynchronous APIs in production, showing how endpoint definitions can drive code generation, schema registration, and the automation of messaging infrastructure.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>
